svg.text: WHAT RUNS WHERE — the server, the database, and everything else
Five tiers. A box belongs to exactly one. The two sentences at the bottom are the whole answer.
icon:
phone /
kiosk
1 · THE HANDSET
The beneficiary's phone, a panchayat kiosk, or an ASHA worker's tablet. NOT a server. NOT a database.
Android app (Capacitor)
· minSdk 24, ~5 MB APK
· Records the mic at 16 kHz mono WAV
· Native Android TTS speaks the prompts
· Tap to start, tap to stop
@rc097/core runs HERE too
The same FSM, ladder, eligibility gate and
recommender that the server runs.
Zero dependencies, so it runs anywhere.
This is why the channels cannot drift.
IndexedDB / SQLite + outbox
A local store with the SAME row shape and
the SAME CHECK constraints as Postgres.
A full interview completes with the radio
off; the outbox syncs itself later.
icon:
cloud /
3rd party
2 · OUTSIDE VENDORS
Not ours. We hold no data here — audio goes out, text comes back, nothing is stored.
Exotel
The phone network. Holds the voice call
and streams 20 ms PCM frames to us.
⚠ AgentStream must be enabled by email
before any of this can be tested.
Meta WhatsApp Cloud API
Delivers the voice note to our webhook
and plays our reply back.
Direct, not through a reseller — no
per-message markup, and audio replies work.
Sarvam — speech to text
saaras:v3. 228-322 ms measured.
22 languages including Maithili.
Our key never leaves our server, so the
handset never talks to Sarvam directly.
icon:
lambda /
function
3 · SERVER — part A: EDGE FUNCTIONS
Supabase, ap-south-1 (Mumbai). Serverless: request in, response out, nothing stays alive between calls.
asr
Takes the recorded WAV, calls Sarvam,
returns the transcript.
HOLDS THE VENDOR KEY. In the APK it
would be one unzip away from anyone.
turn
Two jobs:
· applies the app's offline event list
to Postgres (the outbox drain)
· runs the core for IVR and WhatsApp
This is where DECISIONS are made.
identity
Turns a verified phone number into
hmac(e164, server pepper) = phone_hash.
Returns COUNTS ONLY — never a name,
a trade or an answer.
WHY SERVERLESS IS ENOUGH HERE: every one of these is a single request with a single answer. Nothing needs to stay alive,
so there is no machine to pay for, patch or restart — and it scales to zero between interviews.
icon:
server /
rack
4 · SERVER — part B: ALWAYS-ON VM
Oracle Cloud, Mumbai or Hyderabad. A process that must stay alive. This is the ONLY reason we need a VM at all.
telephony service (Node)
· Holds the Exotel WebSocket OPEN for the whole four-minute call
· Streams 20 ms audio frames both ways, with barge-in
· Receives Meta's WhatsApp webhooks
· Runs @rc097/core — the same code as the phone and the edge function
WHY AN EDGE FUNCTION CANNOT DO THIS
A phone call is not a request and a response. It is a connection that stays
open for minutes, pushing audio in both directions the whole time.
Edge functions are short-lived request/response workers. No amount of
configuration changes that shape. So: one small always-on machine.
icon:
database
cylinder
5 · THE DATABASE
Supabase Postgres, ap-south-1 (Mumbai). Stores rows. Enforces rules. Calls nothing. Decides nothing.
What it holds
beneficiary · session · answer
consent_event · recommendation · outcome
qualification · district · block
district_opportunity
perspective_plan (+ lines)
turn_telemetry · app_user
15 tables, live and seeded.
What it REFUSES
A CHECK constraint makes it IMPOSSIBLE to
store a raw transcript against a confirmed
answer. Not a policy — the database will
reject the row.
There is no audio table and no
recording_url column. The absence is
the feature.
The same constraints exist in the
on-device SQLite schema.
Who may read what
Row Level Security, per role:
· a mobiliser sees only her own district
· an officer sees only their district
· a beneficiary never connects at all
The anon key ships inside the APK and is
PUBLIC by design — RLS is what protects
the data, not that string.
THE DATABASE NEVER CALLS ANYTHING. It has no idea Sarvam or Exotel exist. It receives writes from the server, answers reads
from the officer console, and rejects anything that breaks a constraint. Every decision in this system is made in tier 3 or 4.
THE SERVER is the code that DECIDES — the seven questions, the extraction ladder, the eligibility gate, the ranking —
plus the code that talks to vendors on our behalf so a key never ships in an app.
THE DATABASE is the rows that REMAIN, and the rules that refuse bad ones.
The same core runs in three places: the handset, the edge function and the VM. The database runs in exactly one.
WHAT CROSSES EACH BOUNDARY
handset → edge function
a recorded WAV + a locale. Never a name, never a number.
edge function → vendor
the audio only. The key stays behind; the vendor never sees who it belongs to.
handset → edge function
the offline event list, when signal returns. Idempotent, so replaying is harmless.
VM → edge function
the same event list, for IVR and WhatsApp turns.
edge function → database
rows. Beneficiary first, then session — the foreign key demands that order.
database → officer console
aggregates, scoped by RLS to that officer's own district.
NEVER CROSSES ANYWHERE
the raw audio, the raw phone number, and the transcript after confirmation.
